paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Christ is what matters most, and that can change how you see everything else. Paul is in chains, and he says his circumstances have "actually served to advance the gospel" (Philippians 1:12). He even rejoices when Christ is preached by people with false motives, because the point is that Christ is preached (Philippians 1:18). When Christ is your center, a hard season doesn't get the last word.

Then comes the line to read twice: "For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain" (Philippians 1:21). Paul is torn, because being with Christ is "far better indeed," but he says it is more necessary for the Philippians that he remain (Philippians 1:23-24). I think that's a man who isn't running his life for himself anymore. Living and dying both belong to Christ, so Paul can face either one without fear, and I'm still working on being that calm when my timer is five minutes off.

So Paul asks the Philippians to "conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ," standing firm in one spirit and not frightened by those who oppose them (Philippians 1:27-28). He tells them that suffering for Christ has been granted to them too, and that they're in the same struggle he's in (Philippians 1:29-30). That means you don't have to fight for the faith alone, baker. Stand firm with others, keep your eyes on Christ, and let whatever you're walking through be one more place where He's lifted up.
